To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel process control strategy for FDM printing of SMP is proposed and the variable stiffness omni directional joints are fabricated by this novel process.

A novel 3D printing method is presented to print shape memory polymer (SMA) material using fused deposition modeling (FD) The proposed method enables 3D printing of SMA with a wide range of mechanical properties and high repeatability, and can be used for the design and manufacturing of a novel variable stiffness hyper redundant robot.
a novel 3D printing method is proposed for SMP materials, and a novel design and fabrication process is presented for the modular omni directional variable stiffness ball joint.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication and testing of a novel 3D printed SMP joint with variable stiffness, and the application of this joint to a hyper redundant robotic arm.
the development of a novel variable stiffness hyper redundant robot arm using a 3D printed ball joint with variable stiffness and a novel process control in FDM.
the design and fabrication process of a modular variable stiffness omni directional robotic joint.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design of the variable-stiffness joint and the 3D printing fabrication of SMP are both successful.
the proposed SMP based ball joint is a promising design for a variable stiffness joint, especially when a large number of such joints are cascaded to build a hyper redundant robot.
a new design of a variable stiffness omni directional ball joint is proposed and demonstrated by 3D printing of SMP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we successfully developed a 3D printable variable stiffness joint and built a hyper redundant robotic arm with the joints.
a variable stiffness hyper-redundant robotic arm can be fabricated by using 3D printing of SMP.
the design of the variable joint is feasible, and it can be used in the fabrication of a variable stiffness hyper redundancy robotic arm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the variable stiffness robotic arm can be easily built using a 3D printer.
a novel 3D printing method for SMP material is developed.
a variable stiffness joint can be fabricated by a low cost 3D printing method.
